name: Trichostrongylus spp.

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: about 75–95 × 40–50 µm, thin-shelled and elongated, often with a tapering end and advanced cleavage.
Adults are slender intestinal nematodes; eggs have substantial overlap with hookworm-like forms.

transmission.detail: Eggs hatch in the environment; ingestion of infective larvae on contaminated vegetation leads to intestinal adults.

life_cycle.detail: Eggs hatch in the environment; ingestion of infective larvae on contaminated vegetation leads to intestinal adults.

hosts: Definitive: herbivorous mammals and occasionally humans. No intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide livestock-associated foci, including Asian settings.
clinical_significance: Often mild; heavier infections may cause abdominal symptoms, diarrhea and eosinophilia.
diagnostics: Concentration and calibrated wet mounts at 100–400×; larval or molecular work may be needed for confirmation.
differential_diagnosis: Generally longer and more tapered than hookworm eggs, but size and shape overlap prevent an absolute single-feature rule.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Trichostrongylus spp. — Hairworms of herbivores. Often mild; heavier infections may cause abdominal symptoms, diarrhea and eosinophilia.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
